answer: An operator running many aliases therefore burns for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the yarrow quota and the nebula admission check. Because the counters live in the oasis ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. Submission rate is limited to 10 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole army of identities from one uplink. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
